# MIGRATION SPEC — MCP Python SDK v1 → v2

(As given verba

facts.text: The module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` is removed entirely in v2; everything that lived there moves to `mcp.server.mcpserver`. Any `from mcp.server.fastmcp import X` or `import mcp.server.fastmcp` must become `from mcp.server.mcpserver import X`.

The main server class `FastMCP` is renamed to `MCPServer`; `FastMCP` no longer exists under that name anywhere in the package. Every import of it, use as a type annotation, subclass of it, or construction (`FastMCP(...)`) must have the identifier itself changed to `MCPServer` — a real class rename, not just a change of import location.

The `Context` class moves with the rest of the module: `from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context` → `from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context`. However `Context` keeps its own name — nothing else about `Context` changes (its methods, its behavior, or its use as a type annotation elsewhere). Do not rename `Context`.

On the MCP client side, tool metadata objects returned by the SDK change field naming from camelCase to snake_case: `tool.inputSchema` is renamed to `tool.input_schema`. Client code reading `.inputSchema` off a discovered tool object must change.
`ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()` (the class managing calls across a group of client sessions) has a changed calling contract in v2.
Plain `ClientSession.call_tool()` (a single session) is UNCHANGED — do not conflate it with `ClientSessionGroup.call_tool()`.

Internally the SDK's HTTP transport dependency changed from the `httpx` package to `httpx2`. This is purely internal to the SDK and has zero relevance to application code that imports and uses the separate `httpx` package for its own purposes (e.g. its own unrelated HTTP calls); ordinary application-level `httpx` usage must not be flagged.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: the `@mcp.tool()`, `@mcp.resource()`, and `@mcp.prompt()` decorators have identical signature and behavior in v2.

CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: `ctx.error(...)` / `ctx.info(...)` calls that do not pass an `extra=` keyword argument are unchanged. Calls that DO pass `extra=` have a different, changed signature, but plain calls without `extra=` are to be treated as unaffected.
CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: anything imported from `mcp.types` — this subpackage remains aliased and working in v2.
The listed items are the ONLY confirmed changes in this migration; anything not described in the spec is unaffected, including things one might expect to be affected.

Affected sites include ones reached indirectly through a repo's own helper functions and in test files, and also string literals that reference the old module path `mcp.server.fastmcp` (e.g. inside test mocks), which must be updated.
